# AIS-EVAL-06

**Does each eval that classifies (retrieval, answer or abstain, routing, a guard) name its positive class and set a separate threshold on false positives and on false negatives, weighted by what each error costs, rather than relying on F1 or accuracy alone?**

| | |
|---|---|
| Lens | [AI solution lens](ai-solution.md) 0.4.0 |
| Area | EVAL: Evaluation as evidence |
| Default severity | major |
| Decided by | A tool checks presence; a reviewer judges |
| Reads | `elements.ai.evals.positive_class`, `elements.ai.evals.errors` |

## Why it matters

F1 weighs a false positive and a false negative equally, and accuracy hides both behind the majority class. In most designs the two errors cost very differently: an agent that answers confidently from the wrong source does more harm than one that says it does not know. A better F1 bought by trading precision for recall can make a design worse.

## Rule

Every eval whose metric names F1, F-beta, accuracy, precision or recall has positive_class, and errors with both false_positive and false_negative, each with meaning and max_rate. A reviewer checks that the rates reflect the costs, and that any F-beta's beta leans the way the costs do.

## Sources

- C. J. van Rijsbergen, Information Retrieval, 2nd edition (1979), the effectiveness measure from which F1 and F-beta come (`f-measure`)
- NIST AI 600-1, Generative AI Profile (2024) (`nist-600-1`)
- Microsoft, Copilot Studio agent evaluation and its test methods (2026) (`cs-eval`)
